title: Pain-Proof Warm-Up
subtitle: Protect your knees, shoulders, and lower back before every workout
intro: Run this 8–12 minute full-body warm-up before lifting. Move slow, stay pain-free, and stop short of fatigue. The goal is to lubricate joints and wake up stabilizers — not to tire yourself out.
howTo: Do each move in order, 1 round unless noted. Breathe through your nose. If something pinches, reduce the range and try again next session.

sections.name: Hips & Knees
sections.tagline: Wake up glutes, open hips, and protect your knees
sections.howTo: Nurses spend hours on their feet — these moves restore hip control before squats, lunges, and hinges.

exercises.name: Hip Circles
exercises.why: Lubricates the hip joint and preps your body for single-leg work without knee cave-in.
exercises.cue: Hold a wall lightly, make slow controlled circles — no rushing.

exercises.name: Fire Hydrant
exercises.why: Activates glute medius — the muscle that keeps your knee tracking over your toes.
exercises.cue: Keep your spine quiet. Only the knee lifts, not your whole pelvis.

exercises.name: Clamshell
exercises.why: Builds hip external rotation control — critical for knee health during squats and lunges.
exercises.cue: Feet stay stacked. Open the top knee without rolling your hips back.

exercises.name: Quadruped Rock Back
exercises.why: Gently loads knees and ankles through a pain-free range — great before squat patterns.
exercises.cue: Rock your hips back toward your heels. Stop before any knee pinch.

sections.name: Shoulders
sections.tagline: Open the chest and restore shoulder blade control
sections.howTo: Charting and patient care round the shoulders forward. These moves undo that before pressing and rowing.

exercises.name: Angel Drag
exercises.why: Wall-based shoulder blade slides that open the chest and train upward rotation — a nurse favorite.
exercises.cue: Low back stays flat to the wall. Drag your arms up and down like making a snow angel.

exercises.name: Thoracic Rotation
exercises.why: Restores mid-back rotation so your shoulders do not compensate during presses and rows.
exercises.cue: Hand behind head, elbow opens to the ceiling. Hips stay still.

exercises.name: Prone Y Raise
exercises.why: Activates lower traps and rear delts — the posture muscles that keep shoulders down and back.
exercises.cue: Lie face-down, lift arms into a Y, squeeze shoulder blades, lower slow.

sections.name: Lower Back & Core
sections.tagline: Brace the spine before loading it
sections.howTo: Your low back takes load all shift long. These moves teach your core to stabilize before hinges and rows.

exercises.name: Cat-Cow
exercises.why: Mobilizes the entire spine and tells your nervous system it is safe to move into deeper ranges.
exercises.cue: Inhale into cow, exhale into cat. Move one vertebra at a time if you can.

exercises.name: Dead Bug
exercises.why: Trains deep core bracing while your arms and legs move — exactly what heavy lifts demand.
exercises.cue: Press your low back into the floor. Extend opposite arm and leg without arching.

exercises.name: Bird Dog
exercises.why: Builds cross-body stability for your spine — one of the safest low-back prep moves.
exercises.cue: Reach long through fingertips and heel. Hips and shoulders stay level.

exercises.name: Glute Bridge
exercises.why: Wakes up glutes so your low back does not take over during hip thrusts, RDLs, and squats.
exercises.cue: Drive through heels, squeeze at the top, ribs stay down.

sections.name: Full-Body Flow
sections.tagline: Tie it together before your first working set
sections.howTo: Finish with one integrated stretch that hits hips, thoracic spine, and ankles in a single move.

exercises.name: World's Greatest Stretch
exercises.why: The gold-standard full-body opener — hip flexor, hamstring, thoracic rotation, and ankle mobility in one.
exercises.cue: Deep lunge, elbow to floor, open chest to the sky, then straighten the front leg.

closingNote: Then start your workout. Your first working set should feel smoother — not harder. If joints still feel stiff after 12 minutes, add one more round of the area that needs it most.
